compute: GPU 2 (second queue runner), ~8 min per detector, 9 detectors
detector_set: the nine that saturated the OOF curve: stride-8 linear s46/s47/s48, stride-2 pixel-shuffle s46/s47/s48/s49/s50, multi-layer stride-8 s47 (the stronger of the two multi-layer heads)
training: identical recipe to the fold-clean detectors (train-green 20 x 4 flips, 1000 updates, batch 2, AdamW 1e-5/1e-3, wd 1e-4, clip 1, bf16, threshold 0.35) but initialised from the full-data recipe A encoder experiments/fulldata_recipeA_20261028/regression_std_s46/runs/fold99/cpdino_vitb/epoch_20.pt
blend: a, b (log-linear calibration of the 9-detector mean log hex6 to log HEX) and w fitted on ALL 8934 non-leaked OOF rows of base B using the fold-clean detectors' OOF feature (the deployed detectors have no OOF); the LOFO numbers (-0.028 pp mean on B) remain the only honest estimate of the effect
function: deploy/hex6_correction.py: hex6_correction(image_tensor, base_pred) -> corrected_pred; CD and CV untouched; HEX replaced by exp((1-w) log base_HEX + w (a + b log hex6)); fallback to base when fewer than 20 peaks or no bounded cells
unit_test: deploy/test_hex6_correction.py on the 25 annotated images: determinism, finite output, CD/CV unchanged, HEX change bounded, fallback path, and correlation of the deployed detectors' hex6 with the expert-point hex6 (>= 0.5 required) and with GT HEX (reported)
caveat: val-5 F1 of the deployed detectors is information only: the full-data encoder was trained on those images' scalar labels (never their points).
